questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function
questions.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(2,6).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{2}+2 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2x \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(2,6)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(6,2)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(6) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(6))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function Using a Table
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=4,$ we have

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${f}^{-1}(4)=-3$ and ${f}^{′}(-3)=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Derivative Using Properties of Inverse Functions
questions.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(-1),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(-1)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-1))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(-1).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(-1)=x.$ For $x\ne 2,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(-1) & =x \\ f(x) & =-1 \\ \frac{x}{x-2} & =-1 \\ \frac{x}{x-2}\cdot (x-2) & =-1\cdot (x-2) \\ \frac{x}{\cancel{(x-2)}}\cdot \cancel{(x-2)} & =-x+2 \\ x & =-x+2 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(-1)=1.$

Now we calculate ${f}^{′}(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{x-2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{2}{{(1-2)}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(-1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
